newsitem.title: USA: Coleman closing some plants, cutting jobs.
newsitem.headline: Coleman closing some plants, cutting jobs.

text.p: The Coleman Co, a manufacturer of camping, leisure and other products that posted a $42 million net loss last year, said it was closing some plants, cutting jobs and revamping its product lines to improve its profitability.
The drastic moves include closing and consolidating one international and three domestic factories and cutting its workforce of 7,000 by about 10 percent, it said.
The company said it was also closing its corporate and regional headquarters here and Geneva, Switzerland and moving administrative staff to other offices.
In addition, it said it will eliminate about one-third of the so-called stock-keeping-unit items in the company's product lines.
This is expected to reduce by about $100 million, revenues that produce little or no profit because the products are costly to bring to the market, a company spokesman said.
It said it will also attempt to improve its liquidity by $100 million, primarily through a reduction in working capital and would sell its pressure-washer businesses.
The company spokesman declined to provide details of their working capital reduction plan but said Coleman will release more information in due time.

Jerry Levin, who was named chairman and chief executive officer of the company in February, said Coleman will take additional steps over the course of this year to enhance its position in the recreational and home products markets.
"Going forward, we will further scrutinize every one of our businesses to improve efficiency and reduce costs, Levin said.
At the same time, Coleman will continue working to increase its market share, develop new technologically advanced products and expand globalization with a variety of initiatives, he said.
